claims.subject: perspective:A-PNPR
claims.text: Pedro Albizu Campos: Los imperios ocupan pueblos indefensos a cañonazos, a metralla, con gases venenosos o con vacuna, la cuestión es posesionarse de la riqueza del país y matar a sus habitantes. Literal translation: Empires occupy defenceless peoples with cannon fire, with grapeshot, with poison gas or with vaccine; the point is to take possession of the country's wealth and kill its inhabitants. Working translation: Empires take over defenceless nations with artillery, gunfire, poison gas or vaccination. What they want is the country's wealth, and they kill its people to get it. (GASPI working translation) Context: Quoted by philosopher Carlos Rojas Osorio, who cites it as "Acosta, 123." Rojas Osorio adds that Albizu believed there was a will to exterminate the island's population and denounced the federal government's Malthusian policy in Puerto Rico.

claims.subject: perspective:A-PNPR
claims.text: Pedro Albizu Campos: Es una insensatez creer que los invasores tengan otro interés que no sea la explotación de Puerto Rico. Literal translation: It is foolishness to believe that the invaders have any interest other than the exploitation of Puerto Rico. Working translation: It is foolish to think the occupiers want anything from Puerto Rico except to exploit it. (GASPI working translation) Context: Quoted by Rojas Osorio from Albizu's collected writings (cited as "Albizu, I, 196").

claims.subject: perspective:A-PNPR
claims.text: Pedro Albizu Campos: When our women lose the transcendental and divine concept that they are not only mothers of their children but mothers of all future generations of Puerto Rico, … Puerto Rico will disappear within a generation. (English as published in Laura Briggs, Reproducing Empire (2002). The Spanish original was not available to this project.) Context: Presented in the Dartmouth course essay (S26) as Albizu's answer to writers who blamed Puerto Rico's poverty on overpopulation.

claims.subject: perspective:A-PNP
claims.text: Gov. Pedro R. Pierluisi (PNP): There should be no room in the American family for colonialism, especially when on three occasions in the last decade, a clear majority of the U.S. citizens in Puerto Rico have exercised their right of self-determination in favor of becoming a state of this Union. Context: Written statement to the House Natural Resources Committee, April 14, 2021.

claims.subject: perspective:A-PNP
claims.text: Gov. Pedro R. Pierluisi (PNP): After almost one hundred and twenty-five years of colonial status as a U.S. territory, the American citizens of Puerto Rico favor equality in all respects with their fellow Americans in the fifty states and are ready to begin their own transition to statehood. Context: Same statement.

claims.subject: perspective:A-PNP
claims.text: Gov. Pedro R. Pierluisi (PNP): In Puerto Rico's case, this is not about the mechanism of voting but the denial of that right altogether. Context: On the absence of a vote for President and of voting representation in Congress.

claims.subject: perspective:A-PPD
claims.text: José Luis Dalmau, President, PPD: by excluding the Commonwealth option and its official representatives from the Popular Democratic Party, almost half of the electorate is being excluded from the process, raising doubts about the legitimacy of any future vote. Context: Letter to the House Natural Resources Committee, April 13, 2021.

claims.subject: perspective:A-PPD
claims.text: José Luis Dalmau, President, PPD: the position of the Popular Democratic Party is that this bill is a very defective one. It would grant admission of the island as a state by a simple, uninformed majority vote Context: On H.R. 1522, the Puerto Rico Statehood Admission Act. The letter goes on to cite the effect of federal taxes on local revenue and jobs.

claims.subject: perspective:A-PIP
claims.text: Sen. María de Lourdes Santiago (PIP): Puerto Rico's status problem cannot be attributed to Puerto Rico. Puerto Rico has been the victim and the United States has been the perpetrator. Context: Testimony to the House Natural Resources Committee, April 14, 2021.

claims.subject: perspective:A-PIP
claims.text: Sen. María de Lourdes Santiago (PIP): never once has the United States provided the people of Puerto Rico – a distinct Caribbean and Latin American nation- the opportunity to enter into a process that would permit the exercise of the right to self-determination and independence as required by international law Context: Same testimony, citing the ICCPR and General Assembly resolution 1514.

claims.subject: perspective:A-USEXEC
claims.text: Acting Deputy Attorney General Dana Boente: The Department has concluded that the plebiscite ballot is not compatible with these policies, as it is not drafted in a way that ensures that its result will accurately reflect the current popular will of the people of Puerto Rico. Context: Letter of April 13, 2017. "These policies" refers to Executive Order 13183 and the President's Task Force reports of 2005, 2007 and 2011.

claims.subject: perspective:A-USEXEC
claims.text: Acting Deputy Attorney General Dana Boente: under current law, Puerto Ricans have an unconditional statutory right to birthright citizenship. Context: Same letter, objecting to ballot text that called statehood the only option that guarantees citizenship by birth.

claims.subject: perspective:A-USCONG
claims.text: PROMESA, 48 U.S.C. § 2121(b)(2): Congress enacts this chapter pursuant to article IV, section 3 of the Constitution of the United States, which provides Congress the power to dispose of and make all needful rules and regulations for territories. Context: Statutory text, 2016.

findings.subject: legal:puerto-rico:downes-v-bidwell
findings.text: Justice White, concurring: Puerto Rico "was foreign to the United States in a domestic sense, because the island had not been incorporated into the United States, but was merely appurtenant thereto as a possession."
findings.binding_status: Judgment binding; the incorporation theory came from a concurring opinion

findings.subject: legal:puerto-rico:resolution-748-viii
findings.text: Recognised that the people of Puerto Rico "have effectively exercised their right to self-determination" and found that Chapter XI "can no longer be applied"; the U.S. could stop transmitting information.

findings.subject: legal:puerto-rico:puerto-rico-v-sanchez-valle
findings.text: Going back to the "ultimate source" of Puerto Rico's prosecutorial power "reveals, once again, the U. S. Congress."

findings.subject: legal:puerto-rico:decision-concerning-puerto-rico-draft-a-ac-109-2025-l-7-approved-june-16-2025
findings.text: "Reaffirms the inalienable right of the people of Puerto Rico to self-determination and independence in conformity with General Assembly resolution 1514 (XV)" and "Calls again upon the Government of the United States of America to assume its responsibility to promote a process" for exercising that right.
findings.binding_status: Committee resolution; not binding on the United States

disputes.subject: How many people died because of Hurricane María?

parties.claim: Government of Puerto Rico, initial count: 64
Kishore et al., Harvard-led survey (NEJM): 4,645 excess deaths, Sep 20–Dec 31, 2017 (95% CI 793–8,498)
GWU Milken Institute SPH, commissioned by the Government of Puerto Rico: 2,975 excess deaths, Sep 2017–Feb 2018 (95% CI 2,658–3,290); adopted as the official figure Aug 28, 2018
President Donald Trump, Sep 13, 2018: "3000 people did not die in the two hurricanes that hit Puerto Rico."

disputes.notes: How many people died because of Hurricane María?
